# fondof

> From what you learn to what your agent does.

fondof turns what developers learn — or need — into personalised coding skills fitted to a specific repo's stack, conventions, and patterns. Output is a markdown skill file any AI coding agent can use. Craft and hand-off come first; SkillPool is downstream optional proof.

## How it works

1. Paste a URL (YouTube, blog, podcast) or describe a need
2. fondof extracts discrete idea shards from the content
3. Select shards and forge them into a skill fitted to your repo
4. Copy the skill into your agent, apply it to real work, and optionally share the outcome publicly

## Key URLs

- Homepage: https://fondof.netlify.app
- Skill pages: https://fondof.netlify.app/s/[hash]
- Source pages: https://fondof.netlify.app/from/[domain]
- User portfolios: https://fondof.netlify.app/u/[github-login]
- Pool (quality desk): https://fondof.netlify.app/pool
- API: https://fondof-api.trustfall.workers.dev

## API endpoints

- POST /api/ingest — extract ideas from a URL or need
- POST /api/compose — one-shot: ingest → top shards → forge → skill markdown
  Body: `{ "url": "https://youtu.be/...", "repo": "owner/name" }` (or `{ "need": "...", "repo": ... }`)
  `repo` accepts "owner/name", a GitHub URL (frameworks/languages auto-detected), or `{ "name", "frameworks", "languages" }`.
  Compose is private by default; pass `"private": false` for an explicit public share. The response returns `{ "markdown", "ideas", "skillHash", "skillUrl", "sourceUrl", "onChain", ... }` when shared.
  `skillUrl` is a real shareable page (https://fondof.netlify.app/s/{skillHash}) that resolves without on-chain attestation. Responses include `canonicalSources` and `derivedFromSkillHash` when available.
  Pass `"private": true` to keep it private today. Write `markdown` to `.kiro/steering/` or `.cursor/rules/`.
- POST /api/forge — compose a skill from ideas + repo context
- POST /api/publish — optionally attest a public skill on SkillPool
- POST /api/skills/{hash}/share — explicitly share a private draft publicly
- DELETE /api/skills/{hash}/visibility — owner-only hide/unlist
- GET /api/skills — public skill discovery; `sort=impact|outcomes|adapted|recent` gives focused evidence views (not causal impact). Optional `domain`, `framework`, and `language` filters expose topic/stack discovery.
- GET /api/skills/creator/:login — evidence summary for public skills owned by a GitHub login
- GET /api/sources/:domain — list skills forged from a source plus an evidence-backed impact snapshot
- GET /api/sources/:domain/impact — compact source evidence summary for cards/embeds
- GET /api/sources/:domain/badge.svg — embeddable badge
- POST /api/skills/{hash}/use — record a claimed use; signed-in users deduplicate by account, anonymous users can opt into a random browser receipt key; this is not verified impact
- POST /api/skills/{hash}/meta — attach an outcome and optional PR/screenshot; linked PRs remain unverified evidence
- POST /api/skills/{hash}/verify-pr — optionally ask GitHub to confirm a linked public PR exists; confirmation does not prove causality

## Skill lifecycle

Target lifecycle: private draft → explicit public share → optional SkillPool attestation.
The hosted flow is private-first: a draft remains useful without a public page or chain; explicit sharing creates a durable public artifact, and attestation is a separate choice. Evidence is labeled as claimed use, outcome-attached, linked-PR (unverified), or GitHub-confirmed PR (existence confirmed, causality unproven). Craft first, proof second.

## Skill format

Output is standard markdown with these sections:
- # Title
- ## Context (2-4 sentences, names the repo)
- ## Guidance (one pattern + code example)
- ## Anti-patterns (2-4 bullets)
- ## References (source links)

Skills work in .kiro/steering/, .cursor/rules/, CLAUDE.md, or any markdown-aware agent.
